title: VIO-SLAM Benchmark
description: A reproducible head-to-head benchmark of two monocular-inertial SLAM systems, VINS-Fusion and ORB-SLAM3, on EuRoC MH_01_easy, scored with evo.
extraImageAlt: ATE RMSE per run on the common window: VINS-Fusion odometry only and with loop closure, ORB-SLAM3 over 5 headless runs, and the first ORB-SLAM3 run with the viewer on

stats.label: ATE with Loop Closure
stats.detail: VINS-Fusion ATE RMSE 0.181 m → 0.062 m · local drift (RPE) unchanged · EuRoC MH_01_easy, mono + IMU

extraText: Built VINS-Fusion in Docker (ROS Noetic) and ORB-SLAM3 natively on Ubuntu 22.04 with no sudo, porting ORB-SLAM3 to C++17 to build against Pangolin v0.9.6. Wrote a headless ORB-SLAM3 runner so scored runs carry no viewer or recording overhead, and kept the scored runs separate from the visual-only screen recordings shown here (2× speed).

Scored everything with one evo recipe: SE(3) Umeyama alignment, ATE RMSE, and RPE per 1 m (translation and rotation). Compared VINS with loop closure off and on, ran ORB-SLAM3 5 times because it isn't deterministic, and compared both systems on a common time window because ORB-SLAM3 misses the first ~46 s while its IMU initializes.

ORB-SLAM3 over 5 headless runs: ATE 0.075 ± 0.012 m (range 0.058–0.090 m), with 12–36 map resets during start-up. On the common window, both with loop closure, VINS scored 0.060 m vs ORB-SLAM3's 0.075 m mean, effectively a tie on this easy sequence. ORB-SLAM3 has about half the rotational drift (0.12 vs 0.24 deg/m), while VINS tracks from take-off.
Scope: this covers one sequence, the easiest in EuRoC, and 5 ORB-SLAM3 runs give only a rough spread.
